problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 & -3\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{42}$ equal to zero.*

activity_context.topic_title: Finding Determinants Using Row and Column Operations

feedback.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}-6 & 9 & -3 & 3 \\ 2 & -4 & 5 & 1 \\ -3 & -5 & -3 & -3 \\ 1 & 10 & -4 & 5\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left of ${a}_{14}$ equal to zero.*
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the left of ${a}_{14}=3$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-6 & 9 & -3 & 3 \\ 2 & -4 & 5 & 1 \\ -3 & -5 & -3 & -3 \\ 1 & 10 & -4 & 5\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+2{C}_{4} \\ {C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+(-3){C}_{4} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+{C}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 & 3 \\ 4 & -7 & 6 & 1 \\ -9 & 4 & -6 & -3 \\ 11 & -5 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $1$st row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 & 3 \\ 4 & -7 & 6 & 1 \\ -9 & 4 & -6 & -3 \\ 11 & -5 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{1+4}|\begin{aligned}4 & -7 & 6 \\ -9 & 4 & -6 \\ 11 & -5 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3|\begin{aligned}4 & -7 & 6 \\ -9 & 4 & -6 \\ 11 & -5 & 1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$
